svg.title: Computing shared-exclusion atoms by hand: the AND gate
svg.desc: A step-by-step computation of the four MGW atoms of the AND gate at one row: the joint law, the four events and what they exclude, the informative and misinformative values, and Möbius inversion.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: COMPUTING SHARED-EXCLUSION ATOMS BY HAND: THE AND GATE
T = S1 AND S2, fair bits
② The four events at z, and what they exclude
rows in the event; dark: also T = 0
rows in the event; dark: also T = 0
rows in the event; dark: also T = 0
rows in the event; dark: also T = 0
③ Subtract the atoms below each node (Möbius inversion). Logarithms subtract, so their arguments divide:
Red and Unq2 are negative at this row because S2 = 1 lowers the chance of the observed T = 0 from 3/4 to 1/2.
④ Repeat ② and ③ for every row and average with weights p(row) = 1/4 (nats):
The four net atoms add up to 0.5623 nats = Hbin(1/4) = I(S1, S2; T); synergy is the largest atom.
Exact rationals computed by figures/generate_background_pid.py and checked against figures/sxpid_exact.py and the pid-rs reference values.
